newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil down on crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil down on crude losses.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday in active trade on Monday after big losess to crude in the West on Friday, traders said.
"Gas oil is down because of the fall in crude. The market here was looking to the West for support but now it's not there," one trader said.
August swaps were last quoted at $21.55/$21.65 per barrel, down from Friday's $21.85/$21.95 per barrel.
Brokers said August traded to a low of $21.50 before rebounding on buying from Chinese companies. August traded earlier in the day at $21.53, $21.55 and $21.58, they said.
Traders said the market remains weak despite the purchases from Chinese traders in the swaps market.
"Supply is still abuundant," one trader said.
On Friday August Brent crude closed down 57 cents to $18.12 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange in London.
Traders said physical gas oil might fall to below $20.00 per barrel in late trading due to the substaintial loss to crude prices.
In the physical market late Friday a 150,000-barrel cargo traded at 40 cents below Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis with offers on an outright basis heard at $21.30 per barrel.
The swaps jet fuel/gas oil regrade is steady at the $1.70/$2.00 range for August.
Fuel oil swaps was also unchanged in quiet trading with August last quoted at $97.75/$99.00 and September at $98.25/$99.25.
Naphtha was notionally quoted weaker due to the crude losses with August last indicated at $21.70/$22.00 against Friday's $22.00/$22.15.
